question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': If the committee will approve / the new operational budget, / we will begin the project immediately.
options: we will begin the project immediately.
explanation: चरण 1: यह Conditional Type 1 का वाक्य है। चरण 2: नियम के अनुसार, भविष्य की दो घटनाओं के लिए 'If' वाले क्लॉज़ में Simple Present Tense का प्रयोग होता है। चरण 3: Main clause में Simple Future (will/shall) का प्रयोग होता है। चरण 4: अतः 'If the committee will approve' के स्थान पर 'If the committee approves' होना चाहिए।
trick: If, unless, until, when, as soon as के तुरंत बाद वाले हिस्से में कभी 'will' या 'shall' नहीं आता।
tip: 'If' क्लॉज़ में हमेशा Simple Present Tense का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The CEO is responsible for / organizing meetings, delegating tasks, / and to oversee daily operations.
explanation: चरण 1: वाक्य में Parallelism (समानांतर संरचना) का नियम जाँचना है। चरण 2: Preposition 'for' के बाद कार्यों की एक सूची है: 'organizing' (Gerund) और 'delegating' (Gerund)। चरण 3: 'and' के बाद आने वाला तीसरा कार्य भी Gerund (V-ing) फॉर्म में होना चाहिए। चरण 4: अतः 'to oversee' (Infinitive) के स्थान पर 'overseeing' का प्रयोग होगा।
trick: 'And' के पहले और बाद के शब्दों का Grammatical form (जैसे V-ing) बिल्कुल समान होना चाहिए।
tip: सूची (List) में हमेशा Parallel Structure (V-ing, V-ing, and V-ing) बनाए रखें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Walking across the deserted parking lot, / the stolen vehicle was spotted / by the vigilant night guard.
options: Walking across the deserted parking lot,
answer: Walking across the deserted parking lot,
explanation: चरण 1: यह Dangling Modifier की त्रुटि है। चरण 2: 'Walking across...' एक Participle phrase है। नियमानुसार, इसके ठीक बाद आने वाला Subject ही इस क्रिया को करने वाला (Doer) माना जाता है। चरण 3: यहाँ Subject 'the stolen vehicle' है, जिसका अर्थ निकला कि 'वाहन पार्किंग में टहल रहा था'। चरण 4: सही वाक्य: 'While the guard was walking across the parking lot, the stolen vehicle was spotted...' होगा।
trick: वाक्य के शुरू में 'V-ing' हो, तो कॉमा (,) के तुरंत बाद वाला Subject चेक करें कि क्या वह क्रिया कर सकता है?
tip: Participle phrase के तुरंत बाद उसका सही Subject (Doer) आना चाहिए।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The renowned scientist / not only invented the device / but also the production method.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Not only... but also' का प्रयोग समान Parts of Speech से पहले होना चाहिए (Law of Parallelism)। चरण 2: यहाँ 'but also' के बाद 'the production method' (Noun phrase) है। चरण 3: जबकि 'not only' के बाद 'invented' (Verb) है। चरण 4: संतुलन बनाने के लिए 'not only' को Verb के बाद रखना होगा: 'invented not only the device'।
trick: But also के तुरंत बाद वाला शब्द देखें। Not only को भी ठीक उसी प्रकार के शब्द (Noun/Verb/Adj) के पहले रखें।
tip: Not only और But also के बाद समान Parts of Speech होने चाहिए।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': It is becoming increasingly difficult / for middle-class families / to cope up with inflation.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Cope with' का अर्थ होता है किसी कठिन स्थिति का सामना करना या सामंजस्य बिठाना। चरण 2: भारतीय अंग्रेजी में अक्सर 'cope up with' का प्रयोग कर लिया जाता है, जो व्याकरणिक रूप से अमान्य (Slang) है। चरण 3: इसमें 'up' का प्रयोग Superfluous (अनावश्यक) है। चरण 4: 'cope up with' को 'cope with' में बदलें।
trick: 'Keep up with' सही है, लेकिन 'Cope' के साथ 'up' कभी नहीं आता।
tip: हमेशा 'cope with' का प्रयोग करें, 'cope up with' गलत है।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': If the security team would have / monitored the cameras properly, / the theft could have been prevented.
options: If the security team would have
the theft could have been prevented.
answer: If the security team would have
explanation: चरण 1: Conditional Type 3 (Unreal Past) में 'If' वाले क्लॉज़ में Past Perfect Tense (had + V3) का प्रयोग होता है। चरण 2: Main clause में 'would/could/might have + V3' आता है। चरण 3: 'If' क्लॉज़ में 'would have' का प्रयोग पूर्णतः गलत है। चरण 4: अतः 'would have monitored' के स्थान पर 'had monitored' होगा।
trick: If वाले हिस्से में 'would have' देखते ही उसे 'had' में बदल दें। एक ही वाक्य में दो बार 'would have' नहीं आता।
tip: If clause में Had + V3 और Main clause में Would have + V3 लगाएँ।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The board of directors / only approved a small fraction / of the proposed annual budget.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Only' एक ऐसा Adverb है जो उस शब्द के ठीक पहले आता है जिसकी वह विशेषता बताता है। चरण 2: यहाँ 'only' का प्रयोग 'approved' (मंजूरी दी) से पहले हुआ है, जिसका अर्थ होगा उन्होंने 'केवल मंजूरी दी' (पढ़ा नहीं, चर्चा नहीं की)। चरण 3: जबकि जोर 'a small fraction' पर है। चरण 4: सही क्रम 'approved only a small fraction' होना चाहिए।
trick: Only का स्थान बदलने से वाक्य का अर्थ बदल जाता है। इसे हमेशा मुख्य लक्ष्य (संख्या या वस्तु) के ठीक पहले रखें।
tip: Only को हमेशा उसी शब्द के ठीक पहले रखें जिसे वह modify कर रहा हो।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The leading opposition leader / was falsely accused with / laundering public money through shell companies.
options: laundering public money through shell companies.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Accused' (आरोपी होना) के साथ Fixed Preposition के रूप में हमेशा 'of' का प्रयोग होता है। चरण 2: 'Accused with' या 'Accused for' का प्रयोग व्याकरण के विरुद्ध है। चरण 3: अतः 'accused with' के स्थान पर 'accused of' का प्रयोग करना अनिवार्य है।
trick: Accused of murder. Guilty of theft. Charged with robbery. Accused हमेशा 'of' लेता है।
tip: Accused के बाद हमेशा preposition 'of' का ही प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': You can either choose to / accept the generous severance package / or to face the legal proceedings.
options: or to face the legal proceedings.
answer: or to face the legal proceedings.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Either... or' के प्रयोग में Parallelism (समानता) का नियम लागू होता है। चरण 2: 'either' के बाद 'choose' (Verb) है। 'to accept' Infinitive है। चरण 3: वाक्य की संरचना: 'choose to accept... or to face' में either की स्थिति गलत है। यदि 'either' choose से पहले है, तो 'or' के बाद भी वैसी ही Verb होनी चाहिए। चरण 4: सही संतुलन: 'choose either to accept... or to face...' या 'choose to either accept... or face...' होगा। चूँकि त्रुटि 'either' के स्थान में है, लेकिन यहाँ 'either choose to accept' और 'or to face' असंतुलित हैं। सही रूप: 'either accept... or face' होगा (choose to को कॉमन लें)। त्रुटि 'or to face' वाले भाग में है, इसे 'or face' करना होगा।
trick: Either और Or के ठीक बाद वाले शब्दों का प्रकार बिल्कुल एक जैसा होना चाहिए।
tip: Either...or के बाद हमेशा समान Grammatical Structure बनाए रखें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The newly hired manager / orders his subordinates around / as if he was the CEO of the company.
options: as if he was the CEO of the company.
answer: as if he was the CEO of the company.
explanation: चरण 1: वाक्य वर्तमान की एक कोरी कल्पना (Unreal condition) को दर्शा रहा है ('as if' - मानो जैसे)। चरण 2: Conditional वाक्यों में Subject चाहे Singular हो या Plural, 'As if' क्लॉज़ में हमेशा Subjunctive mood 'were' का प्रयोग होता है। चरण 3: 'was' का प्रयोग यहाँ गलत है। चरण 4: 'as if he were the CEO' सही रूप होगा।
trick: If, I wish, As if से शुरू होने वाले काल्पनिक वाक्यों में 'was' कभी नहीं आता, सिर्फ 'were' आता है।
tip: काल्पनिक (Imaginary) वाक्यों में Subject के साथ हमेशा 'were' लगाएँ।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Having reviewed all the financial documents / meticulously and thoroughly, / the auditor submitted his final report.
options: Having reviewed all the financial documents
the auditor submitted his final report.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Having reviewed...' एक Perfect Participle phrase है। चरण 2: यह phrase जिसके लिए आया है, वह (the auditor) कॉमा (,) के तुरंत बाद Subject के रूप में मौजूद है। चरण 3: चूँकि 'auditor' ने ही डाक्यूमेंट्स रिव्यु किए हैं, इसलिए यहाँ Dangling Modifier की कोई त्रुटि नहीं है। चरण 4: वाक्य पूर्णतः शुद्ध है।
trick: कॉमा के बाद वाले Subject से पूछें 'क्या तुमने यह काम किया?' यदि उत्तर 'हाँ' है, तो कोई Dangling error नहीं है।
tip: Participle phrase का Doer कॉमा के ठीक बाद होना चाहिए।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The entire diplomatic delegation / is eagerly looking forward to meet / the foreign dignitaries tomorrow.
options: is eagerly looking forward to meet
answer: is eagerly looking forward to meet
explanation: चरण 1: 'Look forward to' एक Phrasal Verb है, जिसमें 'to' एक Preposition का काम करता है, Infinitive (to + V1) का नहीं। चरण 2: Preposition के बाद हमेशा Noun, Pronoun या Gerund (V-ing) आता है। चरण 3: 'to meet' का प्रयोग गलत है। चरण 4: इसे 'looking forward to meeting' में बदलना होगा।
trick: Look forward to, Accustomed to, Addicted to, With a view to - इन सभी के बाद हमेशा V-ing (Gerund) आता है।
tip: Look forward to के बाद हमेशा Verb+ing (Gerund) का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': To completely eliminate urban poverty, / the current economic policies / must be revamped by the ruling government.
options: must be revamped by the ruling government.
explanation: चरण 1: यह Dangling Infinitive का उदाहरण है। 'To completely eliminate...' (ख़त्म करने के लिए) एक उद्देश्य बता रहा है। चरण 2: उद्देश्य किसे पूरा करना है? सरकार को (government)। चरण 3: लेकिन कॉमा के बाद Subject 'the current economic policies' है, जो खुद गरीबी ख़त्म नहीं कर सकतीं। चरण 4: सही वाक्य होगा: 'To completely eliminate urban poverty, the ruling government must revamp the current economic policies.'
trick: Infinitive (To + V1) से वाक्य शुरू हो, तो कॉमा के बाद वो इंसान/चीज़ होनी चाहिए जो वह काम कर सके।
tip: Infinitive phrase के बाद उसका तार्किक (logical) Subject रखें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The newly constituted advisory panel / comprises of five eminent experts / from different industrial sectors.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Comprise' का अर्थ होता है 'से मिलकर बना होना' (Consist of)। चरण 2: Active voice में 'comprise' के बाद किसी भी preposition ('of') का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता है। (Passive voice में 'is comprised of' सही होता है)। चरण 3: 'comprises of' गलत है। चरण 4: इसे सिर्फ 'comprises five eminent experts' लिखना चाहिए।
trick: Comprise = Consist of. इसलिए Comprise के साथ 'of' लगाना Superfluous (अनावश्यक) है।
tip: Active Voice में Comprise के साथ 'of' का प्रयोग कभी न करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Both the central government / as well as the state authorities / must collaborate on this sensitive issue.
options: as well as the state authorities
must collaborate on this sensitive issue.
answer: as well as the state authorities
explanation: चरण 1: 'Both' एक Correlative Conjunction है जो हमेशा एक जोड़े (pair) में काम करता है। चरण 2: 'Both' का सही जोड़ीदार 'and' होता है। चरण 3: 'Both' के साथ 'as well as', 'along with' या 'or' का प्रयोग पूर्णतः अमान्य है। चरण 4: 'as well as' को हटाकर 'and' का प्रयोग करना होगा।
trick: वाक्य में 'Both' देखते ही तुरंत उसका जोड़ीदार ढूँढें। वह सिर्फ और सिर्फ 'and' होना चाहिए।
tip: Both के साथ हमेशा conjunction 'and' का ही प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Unless the management does not / clear the pending wage dues, / the workers will go on an indefinite strike.
options: the workers will go on an indefinite strike.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Unless' (यदि नहीं) और 'Until' (जब तक नहीं) दोनों ही Negative conjunctions हैं। चरण 2: इनके अंदर 'not' का अर्थ पहले से ही समाहित होता है। चरण 3: इसलिए, जिस क्लॉज़ में Unless या Until लगा हो, उसमें अलग से 'not' का प्रयोग नहीं होता। चरण 4: 'does not clear' के स्थान पर 'clears' होना चाहिए।
trick: Unless/Until वाले हिस्से में Not, No, Never का इस्तेमाल एक 'Double Negative' त्रुटि है।
tip: Unless और Until वाले क्लॉज़ में 'not' का प्रयोग वर्जित है।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': She is highly appreciated / for her unparalleled creativity, her analytical skills, / and she communicates effectively.
options: for her unparalleled creativity, her analytical skills,
explanation: चरण 1: Parallelism (समानांतर संरचना) का नियम लागू होता है। चरण 2: 'and' से पहले दो Noun phrases ('her unparalleled creativity', 'her analytical skills') हैं। चरण 3: अतः 'and' के बाद भी Noun phrase आना चाहिए, Clause ('she communicates effectively') नहीं। चरण 4: इसे 'her effective communication' में बदलना होगा।
trick: Noun, Noun, and Noun सही है। Noun, Noun, and Clause गलत है। संरचना का वजन बराबर रखें।
tip: And से जुड़ने वाले सभी शब्दों/वाक्यांशों का स्वरूप समान (Parallel) होना चाहिए।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The young athlete is / not enough experienced to handle / the immense pressure of international tournaments.
options: the immense pressure of international tournaments.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Enough' जब Adjective (विशेषण) के साथ प्रयुक्त होता है, तो वह हमेशा उस Adjective के बाद आता है (जैसे- smart enough)। चरण 2: यहाँ 'experienced' एक Adjective है। चरण 3: इसलिए 'enough experienced' लिखना गलत है। चरण 4: सही क्रम 'experienced enough' होगा। (ध्यान दें: Noun के साथ यह पहले आता है, जैसे- enough money)।
trick: Adjective + Enough + Noun. (Enough Adjective के पीछे और Noun के आगे लगता है)।
tip: Enough का प्रयोग हमेशा Adjective के बाद और Noun से पहले करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The heavy barricades at the venue / completely prevented the violent mob / to enter the restricted premises.
options: The heavy barricades at the venue
explanation: चरण 1: 'Prevent', 'Prohibit', 'Stop', 'Abstain' जैसे शब्दों (रोकने का भाव) के बाद Fixed Preposition 'from' का प्रयोग होता है। चरण 2: Preposition 'from' के बाद Verb की 'ing' (Gerund) फॉर्म आती है। चरण 3: यहाँ Infinitive 'to enter' का प्रयोग गलत है। चरण 4: सही संरचना 'from entering' होगी।
trick: 'Prevent' का अर्थ है किसी को किसी काम से रोकना। 'से' के लिए 'from' आता है, और from के बाद V-ing.
tip: Prevent / Prohibit के बाद हमेशा 'from + V-ing' का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Had the intelligence agency acted / on the anonymous tip earlier, / the massive tragedy could have been averted.
options: the massive tragedy could have been averted.
explanation: चरण 1: यह Conditional Type 3 का Inversion रूप है। 'If the agency had acted...' को 'Had the agency acted...' लिखा जा सकता है। चरण 2: 'If' को हटाकर 'Had' को Subject से पहले रखा गया है, जो पूर्णतः शुद्ध है। चरण 3: Main clause में 'could have + V3' (been averted) का प्रयोग भी नियमानुसार सही है। चरण 4: वाक्य में कोई त्रुटि नहीं है।
trick: Had + Subject + V3 ... Subject + would/could have + V3 एक बिल्कुल सही उन्नत (advanced) संरचना है।
tip: Conditional Type 3 में 'If' हटाकर 'Had' से वाक्य शुरू किया जा सकता है।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Due to extreme exhaustion / and severe dehydration, the marathon runner / passed away right before the finish line.
options: and severe dehydration, the marathon runner
passed away right before the finish line.
answer: passed away right before the finish line.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Pass away' का अर्थ है 'मर जाना' (to die)। चरण 2: 'Pass out' का अर्थ है 'बेहोश हो जाना' (to faint)। चरण 3: वाक्य के संदर्भ (थकान और डिहाइड्रेशन के कारण फिनिश लाइन के पास) में धावक के बेहोश होने की बात हो रही है, मरने की नहीं (यह अतिशयोक्तिपूर्ण हो जाएगा)। चरण 4: अतः 'passed away' के स्थान पर 'passed out' का प्रयोग उचित होगा।
trick: Pass away (मरना), Pass out (बेहोश होना), Pass by (गुज़रना)। संदर्भ के अनुसार Phrasal Verb चुनें।
tip: बेहोश होने के संदर्भ में 'pass out' का प्रयोग करें, 'pass away' का नहीं।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': At the age of ten, / my grandfather enthusiastically taught me / how to play the classical violin.
options: how to play the classical violin.
explanation: चरण 1: यह Dangling Modifier का एक और रूप है। 'At the age of ten' एक Prepositional phrase है जो समय बता रहा है। चरण 2: कॉमा के तुरंत बाद Subject 'my grandfather' है। इसका शाब्दिक अर्थ हो गया कि 'दादाजी की उम्र 10 साल थी' जब उन्होंने वायलिन सिखाया। चरण 3: यह अतार्किक है। उम्र मेरी 10 साल थी। चरण 4: सही वाक्य: 'When I was ten, my grandfather taught me...' होगा।
trick: वाक्य के शुरू का Phrase हमेशा कॉमा के बाद वाले पहले Noun/Pronoun से जुड़ता है। तार्किकता (logic) चेक करें।
tip: Introductory Phrase के बाद हमेशा उसका सही तार्किक Subject आना चाहिए।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Suppose if the primary server / completely crashes during the presentation, / what alternative backup plan do we have?
options: what alternative backup plan do we have?
explanation: चरण 1: 'Suppose' (मान लीजिए) और 'If' (यदि) दोनों ही शर्त (Condition/Supposition) बताने वाले शब्द हैं। चरण 2: दोनों शब्दों का अर्थ लगभग समान है। चरण 3: इन दोनों का एक साथ प्रयोग करना Superfluous (अनावश्यक दोहराव) है। चरण 4: या तो 'Suppose' का प्रयोग करें या केवल 'If' का। 'Suppose if' पूर्णतः गलत है।
trick: 'Suppose' और 'If' जुड़वाँ भाई हैं जो कभी एक ही म्यान में (एक साथ) नहीं रह सकते।
tip: Suppose और If का प्रयोग एक साथ कभी न करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The clever detective / not only caught the real culprit / but also the missing evidence.
options: not only caught the real culprit
answer: not only caught the real culprit
explanation: चरण 1: 'Not only... but also' में Parallelism का नियम लगता है। चरण 2: यहाँ 'but also' के बाद 'the missing evidence' (Noun Phrase) आया है। चरण 3: 'Not only' के बाद 'caught' (Verb) आया है, जो असंतुलित है। चरण 4: 'caught' को 'not only' से पहले लाना होगा: 'caught not only the real culprit but also the missing evidence'।
trick: But also के तुरंत बाद क्या है? (मोटे तौर पर Noun)। तो Not only के बाद भी Noun ही होना चाहिए। Verb को बाहर निकालें।
tip: Not only और But also के बाद समान Parts of Speech होने चाहिए।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The famous Hollywood actress / is happily married with / a successful orthopedic surgeon.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Married' शब्द जब Passive Voice (is/was married) या Adjective के रूप में प्रयुक्त होता है, तो इसके बाद Fixed Preposition 'to' का प्रयोग होता है। चरण 2: भारतीय भाषाओं के प्रभाव में अक्सर 'with' (के साथ) का प्रयोग कर दिया जाता है, जो गलत है। चरण 3: 'married with' के स्थान पर 'married to' होना चाहिए।
trick: अंग्रेजी में कोई किसी 'के साथ' (with) शादी नहीं करता, बल्कि किसी 'को' (to) शादी करता है। Married to someone.
tip: Married के साथ हमेशा 'to' Preposition का प्रयोग करें, 'with' का नहीं।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The frustrated clients complained / that neither the regional manager / or the support staff helped them.
options: or the support staff helped them.
answer: or the support staff helped them.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Neither' एक Correlative Conjunction है जो हमेशा एक जोड़े में काम करता है। चरण 2: 'Neither' का सही जोड़ीदार 'nor' होता है। चरण 3: 'Either' का जोड़ीदार 'or' होता है। चरण 4: चूँकि वाक्य में 'neither' है, इसलिए 'or' के स्थान पर 'nor' का प्रयोग करना अनिवार्य है।
trick: 'N' वाले के साथ 'N' वाला (Neither - Nor), बिना 'N' वाले के साथ बिना 'N' वाला (Either - Or)।
tip: Neither के साथ हमेशा nor और Either के साथ or का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The government plans to build / new interstate highways, to establish modern hospitals, / and to generate massive employment.
options: new interstate highways, to establish modern hospitals,
explanation: चरण 1: वाक्य में Parallelism का नियम जाँचना है। 'plans' के बाद तीन उद्देश्य बताए गए हैं। चरण 2: पहला: 'to build', दूसरा: 'to establish', तीसरा: 'to generate'। चरण 3: तीनों ही Infinitives (to + V1) के रूप में हैं, जो पूर्णतः संतुलित (parallel) हैं। (ध्यान दें: बाद वाले 'to' को छिपाया भी जा सकता है, पर लिखना भी व्याकरणिक रूप से सही है)। चरण 4: वाक्य में कोई त्रुटि नहीं है।
trick: To + V1, to + V1, and to + V1 एक बेहतरीन और शुद्ध Parallel संरचना है।
tip: List में सभी verbs समान form (Infinitive या Gerund) में होने चाहिए।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Due to the sudden outbreak / of the deadly virus, the organizers / decided to call out the mega event.
options: of the deadly virus, the organizers
decided to call out the mega event.
answer: decided to call out the mega event.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Call out' का अर्थ है किसी को चुनौती देना या जोर से बुलाना। चरण 2: 'Call off' का अर्थ है किसी कार्यक्रम या योजना को रद्द करना (Cancel)। चरण 3: वायरस के फैलने के कारण इवेंट को 'रद्द' किया जाएगा। चरण 4: अतः संदर्भ के अनुसार 'call out' गलत है, सही Phrasal verb 'call off' होगा।
trick: Off का मतलब बंद या दूर होना। किसी चीज़ को Cancel करना 'Call off' होता है।
tip: रद्द (Cancel) करने के अर्थ में हमेशा 'call off' का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The wealthy businessman bought / a pure leather collar for his pet dog / with pure gold studs.
options: a pure leather collar for his pet dog
explanation: चरण 1: 'with pure gold studs' (शुद्ध सोने के स्टड्स के साथ) एक Modifier phrase है। चरण 2: यह 'collar' (पट्टे) की विशेषता बता रहा है। चरण 3: लेकिन इसे 'dog' के ठीक बाद रखा गया है, जिससे अर्थ निकल रहा है कि 'कुत्ते के शरीर पर सोने के स्टड्स लगे हैं', जो हास्यास्पद है। चरण 4: सही क्रम: 'bought a pure leather collar with pure gold studs for his pet dog' होना चाहिए।
trick: जो Phrase जिसकी विशेषता बताता है, उसे उसी शब्द के बिल्कुल करीब (chipka kar) रखना चाहिए।
tip: Modifier Phrase को हमेशा उसी Noun के पास रखें जिसे वह modify करता है।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': If the experienced architect / had used better quality materials, / the building will be much stronger today.
options: the building will be much stronger today.
answer: the building will be much stronger today.
explanation: चरण 1: यह Mixed Conditional का वाक्य है। 'If' क्लॉज़ में Past Perfect (had used) है, जो अतीत की अवास्तविक स्थिति बता रहा है। चरण 2: Main clause का परिणाम वर्तमान (today) में है। चरण 3: ऐसे वाक्यों में Main clause में 'would + V1' (या would be) का प्रयोग होता है, 'will' का नहीं। चरण 4: 'will be' के स्थान पर 'would be' का प्रयोग होगा।
trick: If + Past Perfect ... Subject + Would (वर्तमान परिणाम के लिए)। पास्ट की शर्त का वर्तमान परिणाम 'would' से दर्शाते हैं।
tip: अतीत की शर्त का वर्तमान परिणाम दर्शाने के लिए 'would + V1' का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The strict high school principal / was extremely angry on the students / for intentionally breaking the glass window.
options: was extremely angry on the students
for intentionally breaking the glass window.
answer: was extremely angry on the students
explanation: चरण 1: 'Angry' (नाराज़) शब्द के साथ अलग-अलग Prepositions आते हैं। चरण 2: जब किसी 'स्थिति या बात' पर नाराज़गी हो, तो 'Angry at' आता है। चरण 3: जब किसी 'व्यक्ति' से नाराज़गी हो, तो 'Angry with' का प्रयोग होता है। 'Angry on' कभी नहीं आता। चरण 4: चूँकि 'students' व्यक्ति हैं, इसलिए 'angry with' सही होगा।
trick: व्यक्ति के साथ (with a person), स्थिति पर (at a thing)। On का कोई काम नहीं।
tip: किसी व्यक्ति से नाराज़ होने पर हमेशा 'angry with' का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The retired professor loved / to write historical novels, to tend his garden, / and spending time with his grandchildren.
options: to write historical novels, to tend his garden,
and spending time with his grandchildren.
answer: and spending time with his grandchildren.
explanation: चरण 1: Parallelism के अनुसार एक सूची (list) के सभी अवयव समान रूप में होने चाहिए। चरण 2: पहले दो काम Infinitives हैं ('to write', 'to tend')। चरण 3: तीसरा काम 'spending' एक Gerund (V-ing) है, जो लय को तोड़ रहा है। चरण 4: इसे Infinitive 'to spend' या केवल 'spend' में बदलना होगा ताकि समानता बनी रहे।
trick: To V1, To V1, and To V1. यदि आखिरी वाला V-ing है तो उसे भी To V1 बनाएँ।
tip: समानांतर संरचना में Active/Passive और Verb Form दोनों की समानता बनाए रखें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Being a severely cold / and heavily foggy morning, the authorities / decided to close all the primary schools.
options: and heavily foggy morning, the authorities
decided to close all the primary schools.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Being a severely cold... morning' एक Participle phrase है। चरण 2: कॉमा के बाद Subject 'the authorities' है। इसका अर्थ निकलेगा कि 'अधिकारी खुद एक ठंडी सुबह थे', जो बेतुका है। चरण 3: मौसम, दिन, या समय के लिए Subject के रूप में 'It' का प्रयोग अनिवार्य है। चरण 4: सही संरचना 'It being a severely cold...' होगी।
trick: जब भी वाक्य 'Being a rainy day/holiday/morning' से शुरू हो, तो उसके आगे 'It' लगाना कभी न भूलें।
tip: मौसम या समय बताने वाले Participle phrase से पहले 'It' का प्रयोग अवश्य करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Though the visiting team played / aggressively throughout the entire match, / but they lost the finals.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Though' और 'Although' विरोधाभास दर्शाने वाले Conjunctions हैं। चरण 2: इनके साथ Correlative pair के रूप में 'yet' का प्रयोग होता है, या केवल एक कॉमा (,) लगाया जाता है। चरण 3: इनके साथ 'but' का प्रयोग व्याकरणिक रूप से पूर्णतः अमान्य है। चरण 4: 'but' को हटाकर 'yet' लगाएँ या केवल कॉमा रहने दें।
trick: Although/Though और But एक दूसरे के कट्टर दुश्मन हैं, ये एक ही वाक्य में कभी साथ नहीं रह सकते।
tip: Though या Although के साथ हमेशा 'yet' या कॉमा (,) का प्रयोग करें, 'but' का नहीं।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The municipal corporation / was strictly instructed to / completely dispose off the toxic industrial waste.
options: completely dispose off the toxic industrial waste.
answer: completely dispose off the toxic industrial waste.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Dispose of' एक Phrasal Verb है जिसका अर्थ है किसी चीज़ से छुटकारा पाना (Get rid of)। चरण 2: यह एक आम भ्रांति है कि इसमें 'off' (डबल f) आता है। व्याकरण में यह हमेशा 'of' (सिंगल f) होता है। चरण 3: 'dispose off' लिखना Spelling/Phrasal Verb की एक क्लासिक त्रुटि है। चरण 4: 'off' को 'of' में बदलें।
trick: Dispose को डबल 'f' (off) से सख़्त नफ़रत है। यह हमेशा सिंगल 'f' (of) लेता है।
tip: छुटकारा पाने के अर्थ में हमेशा 'dispose of' लिखें, 'dispose off' नहीं।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The renowned investigative journalist / has been tasked to systematically / look at the massive financial scam.
options: look at the massive financial scam.
answer: look at the massive financial scam.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Look at' का अर्थ होता है किसी चीज़ की ओर देखना (घूरना)। चरण 2: 'Look into' का अर्थ होता है किसी मामले की गहराई से जाँच-पड़ताल करना (Investigate)। चरण 3: वाक्य में वित्तीय घोटाले की 'जाँच' की बात हो रही है, 'देखने' की नहीं। चरण 4: अतः 'look at' के स्थान पर 'look into' का प्रयोग उचित होगा।
trick: पुलिस या जाँच एजेंसी हमेशा मामले के अंदर (into) देखती है। Look into = Investigate.
tip: जाँच-पड़ताल करने के संदर्भ में हमेशा 'look into' का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The tired and hungry hiker / almost walked twenty miles / through the dense forest before finding the camp.
options: through the dense forest before finding the camp.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Almost' एक Adverb है जो उस शब्द के ठीक पहले आना चाहिए जिसकी वह विशेषता बता रहा है। चरण 2: यहाँ 'almost' को 'walked' (चलने) के पहले रखा गया है, जिसका अर्थ होगा कि उसने 'चलने का काम लगभग किया' (यानी चला ही नहीं)। चरण 3: जबकि अर्थ 'लगभग बीस मील' है। चरण 4: सही क्रम 'walked almost twenty miles' होना चाहिए।
trick: Almost, Only, Even, Just जैसे शब्दों को हमेशा उस Noun/Number के चिपक कर (पहले) रखें जिसे वे Modify कर रहे हों।
tip: Almost को हमेशा उसी शब्द/संख्या के ठीक पहले रखें जिसे वह modify करता है।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The introverted teenager / would rather spend his entire weekend reading fiction / than to attend crowded parties.
options: would rather spend his entire weekend reading fiction
explanation: चरण 1: 'Would rather... than' के प्रयोग में Parallelism का नियम लगता है। चरण 2: 'Would rather' के बाद Bare Infinitive (V1 बिना to के) 'spend' आया है। चरण 3: 'than' के बाद भी Bare Infinitive आना चाहिए। चरण 4: 'than to attend' में 'to' का प्रयोग गलत है। इसे सिर्फ 'than attend' होना चाहिए।
trick: Would rather के बाद V1 आता है, तो than के बाद भी सिर्फ V1 आएगा, 'to V1' नहीं।
tip: Would rather... than के दोनों तरफ Bare Infinitive (V1) का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Not only did the startup / secure substantial series funding, / but it also acquired its main competitor.
options: but it also acquired its main competitor.
explanation: चरण 1: जब वाक्य 'Not only' से शुरू होता है, तो Law of Inversion लागू होता है (यानी Helping Verb Subject से पहले आती है)। चरण 2: 'Not only did the startup secure' पूर्णतः शुद्ध Inversion है। चरण 3: 'but it also acquired' में भी 'but also' का प्रयोग सही ढंग से Verb (acquired) को जोड़ रहा है। चरण 4: अतः वाक्य में कोई व्याकरणिक त्रुटि नहीं है।
trick: Not only शुरू में हो तो 'Helping Verb + Subject' खोजें। यदि वह है, तो वाक्य अक्सर 'No Error' होता है।
tip: वाक्य के 'Not only' से शुरू होने पर Inversion (Auxiliary + Subject) का प्रयोग सही होता है।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The lonely young man / gradually became completely addicted with / gambling and lost his entire family fortune.
options: gambling and lost his entire family fortune.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Addicted' (लत लग जाना) एक Adjective/Participle है जिसके साथ Fixed Preposition का प्रयोग होता है। चरण 2: 'Addicted' के बाद हमेशा 'to' का प्रयोग होता है, 'with' या 'in' का नहीं। चरण 3: इसके बाद आने वाली Verb 'ing' (Gerund) फॉर्म में होती है (to gambling)। चरण 4: अतः 'addicted with' के स्थान पर 'addicted to' होगा।
trick: Addicted, Accustomed, Habituated - इन सभी आदत/लत बताने वाले शब्दों के साथ 'to' आता है।
tip: Addicted के साथ हमेशा Preposition 'to' का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': While crossing the busy intersection, / a speeding delivery truck / almost hit the elderly pedestrian.
explanation: चरण 1: 'While crossing...' एक Elliptical clause है जिसका Subject छिपा हुआ है। चरण 2: नियमानुसार, इसका Subject वही माना जाता है जो कॉमा के बाद मुख्य वाक्य का Subject होता है। चरण 3: यहाँ Subject 'a speeding delivery truck' है, जिसका अर्थ निकला कि 'ट्रक चौराहा पार कर रहा था' (जबकि पैदल यात्री कर रहा था)। चरण 4: सही वाक्य: 'While the elderly pedestrian was crossing..., a speeding truck almost hit him.'
trick: While V-ing के बाद वही Subject आना चाहिए जो वह क्रिया (crossing) कर रहा हो।
tip: While वाले Phrase के तुरंत बाद उसका तार्किक Subject (Doer) रखें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Scarcely had the chief guest / stepped onto the beautifully decorated podium / than the power supply went out.
options: stepped onto the beautifully decorated podium
than the power supply went out.
answer: than the power supply went out.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Scarcely', 'Hardly' और 'Barely' का अर्थ है 'मुश्किल से'। चरण 2: इन शब्दों के साथ Correlative Conjunction के रूप में हमेशा 'when' या 'before' का प्रयोग होता है। चरण 3: 'than' का प्रयोग 'No sooner' के साथ होता है, 'Scarcely' के साथ नहीं। चरण 4: अतः 'than' को 'when' में बदलना होगा।
trick: Scarcely/Hardly के अंत में 'y' (ध्वनि 'इ' / 'क') है, इनका जोड़ीदार 'When' है। Sooner में 'er' है, उसका 'than' है।
tip: Scarcely और Hardly के साथ हमेशा 'when' का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': But for your generous / and timely financial assistance, / my ambitious project will have failed completely.
options: my ambitious project will have failed completely.
answer: my ambitious project will have failed completely.
explanation: चरण 1: 'But for' का अर्थ है 'Without' (के बिना)। यह Past Unreal Conditional (Type 3) को दर्शाता है (यदि तुम्हारी मदद न मिली होती...)। चरण 2: चूँकि यह अतीत की अवास्तविक स्थिति है, Main clause में 'would have + V3' का प्रयोग होना चाहिए। चरण 3: 'will have' का प्रयोग यहाँ गलत है। चरण 4: 'will have failed' को 'would have failed' में बदलें।
trick: 'But for' वाले वाक्यों में हमेशा अतीत की बात होती है, इसलिए आगे 'would have / could have' ही आता है।
tip: 'But for' (बिना) वाले वाक्यों में 'would have + V3' का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The overall literacy rate / in the southern states is significantly / higher than the northern states.
options: in the southern states is significantly
explanation: चरण 1: तुलना हमेशा समान चीज़ों के बीच होनी चाहिए (Illogical Comparison)। चरण 2: यहाँ 'दक्षिणी राज्यों की साक्षरता दर' की तुलना सीधे 'उत्तरी राज्यों' (राज्यों) से की जा रही है, जो गलत है। दर की तुलना दर से होनी चाहिए। चरण 3: इसे सही करने के लिए 'that of' का प्रयोग करना होगा। चरण 4: सही संरचना 'higher than that of the northern states' होगी।
trick: X का Y > Z गलत है। X का Y > Z का Y (than that of Z) सही है।
tip: समान चीज़ों की तुलना करने के लिए 'than that of' या 'than those of' का प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The organizing committee / urgently convened a meeting to discuss / about the plummeting quarterly sales figures.
options: urgently convened a meeting to discuss
about the plummeting quarterly sales figures.
answer: about the plummeting quarterly sales figures.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Discuss' और 'Describe' Transitive verbs हैं। चरण 2: इनका अर्थ ही 'talk about' (के बारे में बात करना) होता है। चरण 3: इसलिए इनके तुरंत बाद Object आता है और 'about' का प्रयोग Superfluous (अनावश्यक) माना जाता है। चरण 4: 'discuss about the figures' के स्थान पर 'discuss the figures' होगा।
trick: Discuss के अंदर 'about' पहले से मौजूद है। Discuss about लिखना 'talk about about' लिखने जैसा है।
tip: Verb के रूप में Discuss और Describe के बाद 'about' का प्रयोग न करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The severely injured accident victim / could hardly not breathe / when the emergency paramedics finally arrived.
options: when the emergency paramedics finally arrived.
explanation: चरण 1: 'Hardly' का अर्थ है 'मुश्किल से ही' या 'ना के बराबर'। यह स्वयं एक Negative Adverb है। चरण 2: अंग्रेजी व्याकरण के नियमानुसार, एक ही क्लॉज़ में दो Negative शब्दों (Double Negative) का प्रयोग नहीं किया जाता। चरण 3: 'hardly' और 'not' का एक साथ प्रयोग गलत है। चरण 4: 'not' को हटा दें: 'could hardly breathe' (मुश्किल से ही साँस ले पा रहा था)।
trick: Hardly, Scarcely, Barely, Unless, Until, Forbid, Deny - इन सभी के साथ उसी क्लॉज़ में 'not' कभी नहीं आता।
tip: Hardly (नकारात्मक शब्द) के साथ 'not' का प्रयोग वर्जित है (Double Negative)।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': I am absolutely afraid / I can no longer put up his / excessively arrogant and demanding behavior.
options: I can no longer put up his
answer: I can no longer put up his
explanation: चरण 1: 'सहन करना' या 'बर्दाश्त करना' (Tolerate) के लिए सही Phrasal Verb 'put up with' होता है। चरण 2: 'Put up' का अर्थ होता है कोई चीज़ खड़ी करना या निर्माण करना (जैसे- put up a tent)। चरण 3: यहाँ 'with' missing है, जो कि अर्थ को अधूरा कर रहा है। चरण 4: 'put up his' की जगह 'put up with his' होना चाहिए।
trick: बर्दाश्त करने के लिए 'Put + up + with' तीन शब्दों की Phrasal verb होती है। एक भी शब्द छूटा तो अर्थ बिगड़ जाएगा।
tip: सहन करने (tolerate) के अर्थ में 'put up with' का पूर्ण प्रयोग करें।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': If the central bank / would have lowered the interest rates, / the inflation would have dropped significantly.
options: would have lowered the interest rates,
the inflation would have dropped significantly.
answer: would have lowered the interest rates,
explanation: चरण 1: Conditional sentences में 'If' वाले क्लॉज़ में कभी भी 'would/will/shall' का प्रयोग नहीं होता। चरण 2: यह Type 3 Conditional है, इसलिए 'If' क्लॉज़ में Past Perfect (had + V3) आना चाहिए। चरण 3: Main clause में 'would have' सही है। चरण 4: 'would have lowered' को 'had lowered' में बदलना अनिवार्य है।
trick: एक ही वाक्य के दोनों हिस्सों में 'would have' कभी नहीं आता। 'If' वाले हिस्से का 'would' काटकर 'had' कर दें।
tip: 'If' क्लॉज़ में 'would have' का प्रयोग अमान्य है; 'had + V3' लगाएँ।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The newly elected mayor promised / to eradicate extreme poverty, to improve basic infrastructure, / and lowering the property taxes.
options: to eradicate extreme poverty, to improve basic infrastructure,
explanation: चरण 1: वाक्य में Parallelism (समानांतर संरचना) का नियम जाँचना है। चरण 2: 'promised' के बाद तीन कार्यों की सूची है। चरण 3: पहला 'to eradicate' (Infinitive), दूसरा 'to improve' (Infinitive) है। चरण 4: तीसरा 'lowering' (Gerund) है, जो संतुलन बिगाड़ रहा है। इसे भी Infinitive 'to lower' में बदलना होगा।
trick: To V1, To V1, and ...? यहाँ भी To V1 ही आएगा। 'And' के बाद वाले शब्द को हमेशा पहले वाले शब्दों से मिलाएँ।
tip: List में सभी verbs समान form (Infinitive या Gerund) में होने चाहिए।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Maintaining a balanced nutritional diet, / exercising on a regular daily basis, / and getting sufficient sleep are crucial for health.
options: exercising on a regular daily basis,
and getting sufficient sleep are crucial for health.
explanation: चरण 1: वाक्य में Parallelism का नियम जाँचना है। यहाँ Subject के रूप में तीन कार्यों की सूची है। चरण 2: पहला: 'Maintaining...', दूसरा: 'exercising...', तीसरा: 'and getting...'। चरण 3: तीनों ही Gerunds (V-ing) के रूप में हैं, जो व्याकरणिक रूप से पूर्णतः संतुलित और समानांतर (parallel) हैं। चरण 4: Plural verb 'are' का प्रयोग भी सही है। अतः वाक्य त्रुटिहीन है।
trick: V-ing, V-ing, and V-ing की संरचना हमेशा Parallelism की सबसे शुद्ध कसौटी होती है।
tip: 'And' से जुड़ने वाले सभी Gerunds समान संरचना में होने चाहिए।

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': If the government / will announce the policy, / the markets will rally.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the sentence as a Type 1 Conditional. Step 2: The conditional clause (If-clause) must be in the simple present tense. Step 3: The main clause correctly uses the simple future tense ('will rally'). Step 4: Therefore, 'will announce' must be changed to 'announces'.
trick: The future context of the entire sentence tricks students into using 'will' in the if-clause.
tip: Never use future tense ('will'/'shall') immediately after 'If' or 'Unless'.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The CEO is committed / to improving infrastructure, / enhancing trade, and to boost the economy.
options: enhancing trade, and to boost the economy.
answer: enhancing trade, and to boost the economy.
explanation: Step 1: Check the list of actions for parallel structure. Step 2: The sentence lists 'improving' (gerund) and 'enhancing' (gerund). Step 3: To maintain parallelism, the third element 'to boost' (infinitive) must be changed to the gerund form 'boosting'.
trick: The word 'to' before 'improving' is a preposition, not an infinitive marker, which causes confusion.
tip: All items in a list must share the same grammatical form (parallelism).

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Being a rainy day, / we decided to stay / indoors and watch a movie.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the participle phrase 'Being a rainy day'. Step 2: A participle phrase at the beginning of a sentence must modify the subject of the main clause ('we'). Step 3: Since 'we' cannot be a rainy day, the modifier is dangling. Step 4: Correct it by providing a subject: 'It being a rainy day'.
trick: In spoken English, 'Being a...' is often used loosely without a proper subject reference.
tip: Participle phrases must logically modify the subject of the main clause.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Had the management / took the decision in time, / the strike could have been averted.
options: the strike could have been averted.
explanation: Step 1: Recognize the conditional inversion 'Had the management...'. Step 2: This is a Type 3 conditional structure which requires 'Had + Subject + Past Participle (V3)'. Step 3: The verb 'took' is the simple past (V2). Step 4: Change 'took' to the past participle 'taken'.
trick: Students often fail to recognize inverted conditionals and accept the simple past tense.
tip: Inverted Type 3 conditionals always require the V3 (past participle) form.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The project manager / is looking forward / to meet the delegates.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the phrasal verb 'looking forward to'. Step 2: In this phrase, 'to' functions as a preposition, not as an infinitive marker. Step 3: Prepositions must be followed by a noun or a gerund (V+ing). Step 4: Change 'to meet' to 'to meeting'.
trick: The combination 'to + verb' looks like a standard infinitive, hiding the prepositional nature.
tip: Phrases like 'look forward to' and 'accustomed to' take a gerund (V+ing).

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The professor / not only gave us notes / but also a lengthy assignment.
explanation: Step 1: Analyze the correlative conjunction 'not only... but also'. Step 2: Check the words immediately following each part. 'but also' is followed by a noun phrase ('a lengthy assignment'). Step 3: 'not only' is followed by a verb ('gave'). This breaks parallelism. Step 4: Move 'not only' to correctly balance the sentence: 'gave us not only notes'.
trick: Placing 'not only' before the main verb is common in speech but violates strict parallelism.
tip: Ensure 'not only' and 'but also' precede the exact same parts of speech.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Fascinated by the painting, / the art critic stood there / for an hour.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the introductory participle phrase 'Fascinated by the painting'. Step 2: Check the subject of the main clause ('the art critic'). Step 3: Ask if the critic was fascinated by the painting. Yes, the modifier logically connects. Step 4: The sentence structure is grammatically sound.
trick: Students actively searching for a dangling modifier might falsely assume 'Fascinated' lacks a proper subject.
tip: If the introductory phrase logically describes the subject, there is no error.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Her daily responsibilities / include managing the team / and to coordinate with clients.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the coordinating conjunction 'and'. Step 2: 'and' must connect parallel grammatical structures. Step 3: The first action is a gerund ('managing'). The second is an infinitive ('to coordinate'). Step 4: Change 'to coordinate' to 'coordinating' to match.
trick: Mixing gerunds and infinitives in a list is a subtle parallelism error often overlooked.
tip: Conjunctions like 'and' or 'or' must connect identical grammatical forms.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Unless you / do not apologize, / she will never forgive you.
explanation: Step 1: Note the conjunction 'Unless' at the beginning. Step 2: 'Unless' intrinsically means 'if not' and carries a negative conditional meaning. Step 3: Using 'do not' in the same clause creates a double negative. Step 4: Remove 'do not' and write 'Unless you apologize'.
trick: Translating from native languages often results in adding a redundant 'not' after 'unless'.
tip: Never use negative words (not, never) in the clause following 'unless' or 'until'.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The prime suspect / was accused with / stealing the confidential documents.
explanation: Step 1: Focus on the verb 'accused'. Step 2: In English grammar, certain verbs take fixed prepositions. Step 3: The verb 'accuse' is always followed by the preposition 'of', not 'with'. Step 4: Change 'accused with' to 'accused of'.
trick: The word 'charged' takes 'with' (charged with a crime), tricking candidates into using 'with' for 'accused'.
tip: Remember: 'Accused of' a crime, but 'charged with' a crime.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The newly formed committee / comprises of eminent scholars / and industry experts.
explanation: Step 1: Locate the verb 'comprises'. Step 2: In active voice, the verb 'comprise' means 'consists of' and does not take a preposition. Step 3: The addition of 'of' is redundant. Step 4: Remove 'of' to make it 'comprises eminent scholars'.
trick: Candidates confuse 'comprise' with 'consist of' or the passive structure 'is comprised of'.
tip: Use 'consists of' or 'comprises', but never 'comprises of' in active voice.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': To enter the secure room, / the security door / must be unlocked first.
explanation: Step 1: Check the introductory infinitive phrase 'To enter the secure room'. Step 2: This phrase must logically apply to the subject of the main clause. Step 3: The subject is 'the security door', but a door cannot enter a room. Step 4: Rewrite to give a proper subject, e.g., 'you must unlock the security door'.
trick: The passive voice in the main clause hides the absence of a logical agent for the infinitive.
tip: Introductory infinitive phrases must logically connect to the main clause's subject.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Scarcely had he / stepped out of the house, / than it started raining heavily.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the correlative conjunction 'Scarcely'. Step 2: 'Scarcely' and 'Hardly' are strictly followed by the conjunction 'when' or 'before'. Step 3: The sentence incorrectly uses 'than'. Step 4: Replace 'than' with 'when'.
trick: Because 'No sooner' takes 'than', students often blindly apply 'than' to 'Scarcely' and 'Hardly' as well.
tip: Always pair 'Hardly/Scarcely' with 'when', and 'No sooner' with 'than'.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Suppose if you / miss the last train, / what will you do?
explanation: Step 1: Examine the beginning of the sentence 'Suppose if'. Step 2: Both 'suppose' and 'if' convey the exact same conditional meaning. Step 3: Using them together creates a redundancy error (superfluous expression). Step 4: Drop either 'Suppose' or 'if'.
trick: In informal Indian English, 'suppose if' is frequently used as a combined phrase.
tip: Never use 'suppose' and 'if' together; they mean the same thing.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The factory management / decided to dispose off / all the old machinery.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the phrasal verb phrase 'dispose off'. Step 2: In standard English, the correct phrasal verb meaning to get rid of something is 'dispose of' (with a single 'f'). Step 3: 'Dispose off' is grammatically incorrect. Step 4: Change 'off' to 'of'.
trick: The phonetic similarity and the general use of 'off' for removal makes 'dispose off' seem correct.
tip: Always write 'dispose of', never 'dispose off'.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': She has both / the experience for the job / and the necessary qualifications.
explanation: Step 1: Analyze the correlative conjunction 'both... and'. Step 2: Check for parallel placement. 'and' is followed by a noun phrase ('the necessary qualifications'). Step 3: 'both' should ideally be placed directly before the corresponding noun phrase. Step 4: Move 'both' to read 'She has both the experience... and the qualifications' (no error in structure actually, but if it read 'Both she has...', it would be wrong). Wait, 'has both the experience' is fine. Let's look closer. Actually, 'She has both the experience... and the necessary qualifications' is structurally perfectly parallel. Therefore, there is no error.
trick: Examiners create complex noun phrases to make parallel structures look misaligned when they aren't.
tip: Check if 'both' and 'and' are immediately followed by similar grammatical units.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': He found it difficult / to cope up with / the immense work pressure.
explanation: Step 1: Focus on the phrasal verb 'cope up with'. Step 2: The correct English idiom for managing a difficult situation is 'cope with'. Step 3: The inclusion of 'up' is a common slang error. Step 4: Remove 'up' to make it 'cope with'.
trick: The phrase 'keep up with' causes interference, leading people to wrongly say 'cope up with'.
tip: The correct phrase is 'cope with'; 'cope up with' does not exist.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': He almost ate / all the cookies / left in the jar.
explanation: Step 1: Check the placement of the limiting modifier 'almost'. Step 2: A modifier must be placed as close as possible to the word it modifies. Step 3: 'He almost ate' implies he came close to the act of eating but didn't. The intended meaning is that he ate a quantity close to 'all'. Step 4: Move 'almost' to modify 'all': 'He ate almost all the cookies'.
trick: Colloquially, placing 'almost' before the verb is widely accepted, masking the logical error.
tip: Place limiting modifiers (almost, only, just) directly before the word they modify.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': You must avail of / this golden opportunity / to advance your career.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the verb 'avail'. Step 2: 'Avail' is a transitive verb that strictly requires a reflexive pronoun when used with 'of' to mean taking advantage of something. Step 3: The sentence lacks this pronoun. Step 4: Add the reflexive pronoun 'yourself' to make it 'You must avail yourself of'.
trick: Because 'avail' sounds complete to non-native speakers, the missing reflexive pronoun is hard to spot.
tip: Verbs like avail, pride, and acquit require a reflexive pronoun (myself, yourself).

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Either the manager / will sign the document / or his assistant will.
explanation: Step 1: Examine the correlative conjunction 'Either... or'. Step 2: Check the grammatical unit following each. 'or' is followed by a subject + verb ('his assistant will'). Step 3: 'Either' is followed by a subject ('the manager'), but the verb 'will sign' applies to both. The structure is unbalanced. Step 4: The correct parallel form is 'Either the manager or his assistant will sign...'.
trick: Separating the verb from one of the subjects breaks the necessary parallel framework.
tip: Correlative conjunctions (either/or) must link structurally identical sentence parts.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': If I would have / studied harder, / I would have passed the exam.
options: I would have passed the exam.
explanation: Step 1: The sentence is a Type 3 conditional, discussing an unreal past situation. Step 2: The structure requires 'If + Past Perfect (had + V3)' in the if-clause. Step 3: 'would have' is only used in the main clause. Step 4: Change 'If I would have' to 'If I had'.
trick: The repetition of 'would have' in both clauses feels rhythmically correct but is grammatically wrong.
tip: Never use 'would have' in the 'if' clause of a conditional sentence.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Having finished the assignment, / the students were allowed / to leave the classroom.
explanation: Step 1: Check the perfect participle phrase 'Having finished the assignment'. Step 2: Verify the subject of the main clause ('the students'). Step 3: Did the students finish the assignment? Yes, the modifier correctly attaches to the subject. Step 4: The sentence contains no dangling modifier and is structurally correct.
trick: Test-takers often assume perfect participles ('Having + V3') are inherently problematic.
tip: If the introductory phrase logically modifies the immediate subject, it is correct.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': She told him / to clean his room, / to wash his clothes, and take out the trash.
options: to wash his clothes, and take out the trash.
answer: to wash his clothes, and take out the trash.
explanation: Step 1: Observe the list of commands for parallel structure. Step 2: The items are 'to clean', 'to wash', and 'take'. Step 3: While repeating 'to' is optional, if you repeat it for the second item, you must repeat it for the third, OR drop it for both the second and third. Step 4: Change to 'to wash his clothes, and to take out the trash' or 'wash his clothes, and take...'.
trick: Inconsistent dropping of the infinitive marker 'to' ruins parallel structure.
tip: In a list of infinitives, either use 'to' only once or repeat it every time.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': No sooner had the bell rung / when the children / rushed out of the class.
options: No sooner had the bell rung
explanation: Step 1: Identify the conjunction 'No sooner' at the start. Step 2: The structure 'No sooner... than' is a fixed grammatical pair. Step 3: The sentence incorrectly uses 'when' instead of 'than'. Step 4: Replace 'when' with 'than'.
trick: Because 'Hardly' takes 'when', students frequently mix up the pairings.
tip: Always pair 'No sooner' with 'than'. ('Hardly/Scarcely' takes 'when').

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The teacher was / very angry at the student / for his misbehavior.
explanation: Step 1: Look at the adjective 'angry' and the preposition following it. Step 2: In English grammar, you are angry 'at' a situation or thing, but angry 'with' a person. Step 3: 'the student' is a person. Step 4: Change 'angry at' to 'angry with'.
trick: People commonly say 'angry at someone' in conversational English, hiding the grammatical distinction.
tip: Use 'angry with' for a person and 'angry at' for a thing/situation.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The heavy rain / prevented us to go / to the outdoor concert.
explanation: Step 1: Locate the verb 'prevented'. Step 2: The verb 'prevent' requires a specific prepositional structure: 'prevent someone from doing something'. Step 3: The sentence incorrectly uses the infinitive 'to go'. Step 4: Change 'to go' to 'from going'.
trick: The infinitive 'to go' sounds logical regarding purpose, but 'prevent' dictates its own preposition.
tip: Verbs like prevent, prohibit, and abstain are always followed by 'from + V-ing'.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': But for your timely help, / I would not have / completed this project.
explanation: Step 1: Understand the phrase 'But for'. It means 'If it had not been for' and acts as a past conditional trigger. Step 2: This corresponds to a Type 3 conditional. Step 3: The main clause correctly uses 'would not have + V3' ('would not have completed'). Step 4: The sentence is entirely correct.
trick: Students unfamiliar with the idiom 'But for' might assume it is grammatically disjointed.
tip: The phrase 'But for' means 'without' and correctly pairs with conditional structures.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': While walking across the street, / a speeding bus / knocked him down.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the participle phrase 'While walking across the street'. Step 2: This phrase must modify the subject of the main clause, which is 'a speeding bus'. Step 3: A bus cannot walk across the street; the modifier is dangling. Step 4: Correct it by providing the clear subject: 'While he was walking across the street'.
trick: The object 'him' in the main clause makes it easy to logically infer who was walking, but it's grammatically incorrect.
tip: An introductory phrase with 'while' must logically share the main clause's subject.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': After battling illness / for a long time, / the old man passed out.
explanation: Step 1: Analyze the phrasal verb 'passed out'. Step 2: 'Pass out' means to faint or lose consciousness. Step 3: The context of 'battling illness for a long time' heavily implies death. The phrasal verb for dying is 'passed away'. Step 4: Change 'passed out' to 'passed away'.
trick: Confusing the subtle meanings of phrasal verbs starting with 'pass' is a common vocabulary trap.
tip: 'Pass away' means to die; 'pass out' means to faint.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The delegates entered / into the conference room / to begin the negotiations.
explanation: Step 1: Look at the verb 'entered' and the following preposition 'into'. Step 2: When 'enter' refers to physically moving into a place (like a room or building), it is a transitive verb and takes no preposition. Step 3: 'into' is redundant. Step 4: Remove 'into' to make it 'entered the conference room'.
trick: We 'enter into' an agreement or conversation, but never 'enter into' a physical space.
tip: Omit 'into' when 'enter' means physical entry into a place.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The population of China / is much greater / than India.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the items being compared. The sentence compares 'The population of China' to 'India'. Step 2: This is an illogical comparison. You must compare population to population. Step 3: Instead of repeating 'the population of', use the pronoun 'that of'. Step 4: Change 'than India' to 'than that of India'.
trick: The brain automatically fills in the missing comparative element, hiding the structural flaw.
tip: Always use 'that of' (singular) or 'those of' (plural) to balance comparisons.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': If he calls me, / I will definitely / attend his party.
explanation: Step 1: Verify the conditional structure. This is a Type 1 conditional (real future possibility). Step 2: The if-clause uses the simple present ('calls'). Step 3: The main clause correctly uses the simple future ('will attend'). Step 4: The grammar and structure are perfectly sound.
trick: The presence of the adverb 'definitely' might make students doubt the modal verb placement.
tip: Type 1 conditionals strictly follow: If + Simple Present, Subject + Will + Base Verb.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Work hard / lest you / will fail the examination.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the conjunction 'lest', which means 'to prevent' or 'in case'. Step 2: 'Lest' must always be followed by the modal verb 'should' (or the base form in subjunctive). Step 3: The sentence uses 'will', which is incorrect. Step 4: Replace 'will' with 'should'.
trick: Because the sentence discusses a future consequence, 'will' feels natural but violates the 'lest' rule.
tip: The conjunction 'lest' must always be followed by 'should'.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The manager demanded / that the employee / goes on leave immediately.
explanation: Step 1: Locate the verb 'demanded that'. Step 2: Verbs expressing commands, suggestions, or requests (demand, insist, suggest) trigger the subjunctive mood in the following clause. Step 3: The subjunctive mood requires the base form of the verb, regardless of the subject. Step 4: Change 'goes' to 'go'.
trick: The singular subject 'employee' naturally attracts the singular verb 'goes', masking the subjunctive requirement.
tip: Use the base form of the verb after 'demand that', 'suggest that', or 'insist that'.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': We kindly request you / to bear upon us / while the system is being fixed.
options: while the system is being fixed.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the intended meaning: asking for patience. Step 2: Analyze the phrasal verb 'bear upon'. 'Bear upon' means to have relevance to something. Step 3: The correct phrasal verb for asking someone to be patient is 'bear with'. Step 4: Change 'bear upon' to 'bear with'.
trick: Similar sounding prepositions in phrasal verbs frequently confuse non-native speakers.
tip: 'Bear with me' means 'be patient with me'.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': I congratulated him / for his brilliant success / in the recent examinations.
explanation: Step 1: Note the verb 'congratulated'. Step 2: The verb 'congratulate' takes a specific fixed preposition. Step 3: We congratulate someone 'on' their success, not 'for' their success. Step 4: Replace 'for' with 'on'.
trick: Because we say 'praised for', students incorrectly apply 'for' to 'congratulate'.
tip: Always use 'on' after the verbs congratulate and compliment.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The brilliant student / could only solve / two questions out of ten.
explanation: Step 1: Analyze the placement of the modifier 'only'. Step 2: 'Only' should be placed immediately before the word it modifies to prevent ambiguity. Step 3: Placing it before 'solve' implies restriction on the action (he could only solve, not write). The sentence intends to limit the number. Step 4: Move 'only' to precede 'two': 'could solve only two questions'.
trick: In spoken language, 'only' is often casually placed before the main verb.
tip: Place 'only' directly adjacent to the exact word or phrase it modifies.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The young man / is heavily addicted to / smoke cigarettes.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the phrase 'addicted to'. Step 2: In this phrase, 'to' acts as a preposition, not an infinitive marker. Step 3: Prepositions must be followed by a noun or a gerund (V+ing). Step 4: The base verb 'smoke' must be changed to the gerund 'smoking'.
trick: The combination 'to smoke' looks exactly like a standard infinitive.
tip: Phrases like 'addicted to' and 'prone to' must be followed by an '-ing' form.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': He is not / as intelligent / as his older brother is.
explanation: Step 1: Check the correlative comparison structure. The sentence is negative ('not'). Step 2: While 'as...as' can be used in negative sentences, standard formal grammar strongly prefers 'so...as' for negative comparisons. Step 3: Change 'as intelligent' to 'so intelligent'.
trick: Modern English often accepts 'not as...as', but strict prescriptive exams prefer 'not so...as'.
tip: In negative sentences, prefer the 'so...as' structure over 'as...as'.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The committee members / agreed to the proposal / without any hesitation.
explanation: Step 1: Check the verb 'agreed' and its preposition. Step 2: You agree 'with' a person, but you agree 'to' a proposal or plan. Step 3: The phrase 'agreed to the proposal' correctly follows this rule. Step 4: The sentence is grammatically flawless.
trick: Candidates might think 'agreed with the proposal' is universally required.
tip: Agree 'with' a person; agree 'to' a thing/proposal.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The workers decided / to call for the strike / after their demands were met.
explanation: Step 1: Analyze the meaning of the phrasal verb 'call for'. Step 2: 'Call for' means to demand or require something. Step 3: Since their demands were met, they logically meant to cancel the strike. The phrasal verb for cancel is 'call off'. Step 4: Change 'call for' to 'call off'.
trick: The phrase 'call for a strike' is common, but contextually contradicts 'demands were met'.
tip: 'Call for' means demand; 'call off' means cancel.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': He would rather / surrender to the enemy / than to betray his country.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the structure 'would rather... than'. Step 2: 'Would rather' is followed by a bare infinitive (a verb without 'to') ('surrender'). Step 3: To maintain parallel structure, the verb after 'than' must also be a bare infinitive. Step 4: Change 'to betray' to 'betray'.
trick: The word 'to' creeps in naturally in speech when connecting verb clauses.
tip: The structure 'would rather... than' connects two bare infinitives (no 'to').

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Had he been / more careful, / he would avoid the accident.
explanation: Step 1: The phrase 'Had he been' indicates a Type 3 conditional (unreal past). Step 2: The conditional clause structure is 'Had + Subject + V3'. Step 3: The corresponding main clause must be 'would have + V3'. Step 4: The phrase 'would avoid' is incorrect and must be changed to 'would have avoided'.
trick: The inverted conditional is correct, but the error is cleverly hidden in the main clause.
tip: Type 3 conditionals require 'would have + past participle' in the main clause.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Covered in mud, / she immediately wiped / the dog with a towel.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the participle phrase 'Covered in mud'. Step 2: Check the subject of the main clause, which is 'she'. Step 3: This implies 'she' was covered in mud, but contextually, the dog was covered in mud. Step 4: Restructure to clear the dangling modifier: 'She wiped the dog, which was covered in mud...'.
trick: The mind automatically assigns the modifier 'Covered in mud' to the dog, missing the grammatical link to 'she'.
tip: Participle phrases modify the immediate subject of the main clause.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': I cannot put up / with his constant / complaints anymore.
explanation: Step 1: Check the phrasal verb 'put up with'. Step 2: 'Put up with' means to tolerate or endure something unpleasant. Step 3: The phrase is used correctly in the context of enduring constant complaints. Step 4: There is no grammatical or structural error.
trick: Test-takers often suspect three-part phrasal verbs contain a redundant preposition.
tip: 'Put up with' is a valid, standard phrase meaning 'to tolerate'.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': After dating for years, / she finally got married / with her childhood sweetheart.
explanation: Step 1: Examine the phrase 'got married' and its preposition. Step 2: In English grammar, you get married 'to' someone, not 'with' someone. Step 3: The preposition 'with' is incorrect. Step 4: Change 'with' to 'to'.
trick: In many native languages, the literal translation is 'married with', causing a direct transfer error.
tip: Always use 'married to someone', never 'married with someone'.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': Not only did he break / the valuable vase, / but he also refused to pay.
options: but he also refused to pay.
explanation: Step 1: The sentence begins with the negative adverbial phrase 'Not only'. Step 2: This correctly triggers subject-verb inversion ('did he break'). Step 3: The correlative pair 'but... also' correctly introduces the second independent clause. Step 4: The sentence maintains parallel independent clauses and is grammatically correct.
trick: Candidates often think 'Not only' must be followed immediately by a verb, misunderstanding the inversion rule.
tip: Sentences starting with 'Not only' require auxiliary inversion (did he, is he).

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': At the age of five, / my father passed away / in a tragic accident.
explanation: Step 1: Look at the introductory phrase 'At the age of five'. Step 2: This phrase acts as an adjectival modifier for the subject of the main clause ('my father'). Step 3: This implies the father died when he (the father) was five, which is absurd. Step 4: Fix the dangling modifier by specifying the subject: 'When I was five, my father...'.
trick: Context easily overrides grammar in reading, masking the absurd literal meaning.
tip: Ensure introductory phrases denoting time/age match the subject.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': The detective was hired / to investigate into / the mysterious murder case.
explanation: Step 1: Locate the verb 'investigate'. Step 2: 'Investigate' is a transitive verb that directly takes an object. It means 'to look into'. Step 3: Adding 'into' creates a redundancy. Step 4: Remove the preposition 'into' to make it 'to investigate the mysterious...'.
trick: Because the phrasal verb 'look into' means investigate, people erroneously combine them into 'investigate into'.
tip: Never use the preposition 'into' directly after the verb 'investigate'.

question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error': I would prefer / to stay at home / rather than to go out.
explanation: Step 1: Identify the phrase 'prefer to... rather than'. Step 2: The structure links two actions. The first is a full infinitive ('to stay'). Step 3: After 'rather than', the parallel structure strictly requires a bare infinitive (without 'to'). Step 4: Change 'to go out' to 'go out'.
trick: Parallelism usually dictates repeating 'to', but 'rather than' is an exception requiring a bare infinitive.
tip: Always use a bare infinitive (verb without 'to') after 'rather than'.
